c.tagline: India's Pink City, a royal Rajput capital of forts, bazaars, and rose-hued facades.

taxi.color: Radio cabs are unbranded; auto-rickshaws are green & yellow
taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws rarely use the meter—agree a flat fare before boarding. App cabs (Uber/Ola) and bike/auto app Rapido are metered and the simplest way to avoid haggling.

emergency.note: 112 is India's unified emergency number; 100 reaches police, 108 ambulance, and 101 fire directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Aggressive touts and commission scams at the forts; gem-export and "government emporium" scams

hood_desc: The walled historic core painted terracotta-pink, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, and the buzzing bazaars of Johari and Bapu; best for first-timers who want the landmarks and markets on their doorstep.

Jaipur's upscale, leafy modern quarter around Statue Circle and Ashok Marg, packed with fine-dining restaurants, cafes, bars, and boutiques; suits travelers who want a cosmopolitan base with the city's best nightlife and dining.

A calm, green residential neighborhood of heritage guesthouses and boutique hotels, walkable to the railway station and Sindhi Camp bus stand; ideal for a peaceful, well-connected base close to the sights.
A quiet, orderly area of tree-lined avenues, government bungalows, and embassies west of the old city; good for a relaxed, upscale stay away from the crowds, with the metro and MI Road nearby.
Jaipur's main commercial artery linking the old city to the new, lined with shops, showrooms, banks, restaurants, and famous sweet shops; a convenient, central base for shopping and eating.
lodging: Umaid Bhawan - A Heritage Style Boutique Hotel

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only; avoid ice of unknown origin.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable metro Smart Card at any station counter for about ₹100 (~$1, including a ₹50 refundable deposit) for a 10% fare discount, or pay per ride with a token/QR ticket; single fares run ₹10-30 (~$0.10-0.30). JCTSL city buses take cash to the conductor (₹10-25); there is no unified city-wide transit card as of 2026.
transit.hours: The metro Pink Line runs roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM with trains every 10-15 minutes; city buses run from about 6:00 AM to 9:30 PM.
transit.note: The metro is a single Pink Line (Mansarovar to Badi Chaupar) mainly useful along that corridor, so most getting-around is by auto-rickshaw, app cabs (Uber/Ola), the Rapido bike/auto app, and JCTSL buses.

transit.m: Prepaid taxi or Uber/Ola to the Pink City (20-30 min)
Auto-rickshaw to central Jaipur / MI Road (~25-30 min)
JCTSL city bus toward Ajmeri Gate / MI Road area

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated. Many upscale places already add a service charge, so check the bill first.

food.name: Dal baati churma
food.desc: Baked wheat balls cracked open and soaked in ghee, eaten with spiced lentils and sweet crushed churma - Rajasthan on one plate.

places.name: Chokhi Dhani
places.note: Village-themed resort serving the full Rajasthani thali; touristy but the food is the real thing.

places.name: Spice Court
places.note: Garden restaurant in a colonial bungalow, long a reliable address for Rajasthani classics.

places.name: Natraj Restaurant
places.note: Vegetarian institution on MI Road with a strong reputation among Jaipur families.

food.name: Laal maas
food.desc: Mutton stewed in a searing gravy of Mathania red chillies, garlic and yoghurt - the royal hunting dish of Rajasthan.

places.name: Handi Restaurant
places.note: Smoky, no-frills MI Road legend; widely named the city's best laal maas and safed maas.

places.name: 1135 AD
places.note: Opulent dining inside Amber Fort; heritage Rajput recipes in a spectacular setting.

places.name: Spice Court
places.note: Milder, well-executed version for those who want the dish without the full chilli assault.

food.name: Pyaaz kachori
food.desc: A flaky fried pastry stuffed with spiced onion masala, cracked open and doused in tamarind and mint chutney.

places.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
places.note: The city's most famous kachori counter; go early, they sell out through the morning.

places.name: Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB)
places.note: Old-city sweet shop and restaurant running since 1727; a Jaipur landmark in its own right.

places.name: Samrat Restaurant
places.note: Long-running vegetarian spot handy for kachoris and thalis in the new city.

food.name: Ghewar
food.desc: A honeycombed disc of fried batter soaked in sugar syrup and topped with rabri and pistachio, made for Teej and Rakhi.

places.name: Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB)
places.note: Perhaps the best-known ghewar in India; also try the paneer ghewar and ghewar rabri.

places.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
places.note: Famous for mawa kachori as well as seasonal ghewar; boxes travel well.

places.name: Sodhani Sweets
places.note: Respected Jaipur mithai maker with a strong local following for festival sweets.

food.name: Gatte ki sabzi
food.desc: Gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yoghurt gravy - desert cooking born of a place with almost no fresh vegetables.

places.name: Natraj Restaurant
places.note: Vegetarian mainstay that cooks the everyday Rajasthani repertoire properly.

places.name: Santhosh Bhojnalaya
places.note: Plain old-city bhojnalaya serving unlimited Rajasthani thalis at local prices.

places.name: Chokhi Dhani
places.note: Part of the endless thali, served on leaf plates with folk music and camel rides.

food.name: Ker sangri
food.desc: Dried desert berries and beans rehydrated and tempered with chilli, asafoetida and plenty of ghee - intensely tangy and unique to Rajasthan.

places.name: Suvarna Mahal
places.note: Grand palace dining room reviving royal Rajasthani recipes; special-occasion territory.

places.name: 1135 AD
places.note: Heritage menu inside the fort walls, including hard-to-find desert vegetable dishes.

places.name: Chokhi Dhani
places.note: Included in the traditional thali; the easiest way to try it without a big spend.

food.name: Lassi
food.desc: Thick sweet curd whipped with sugar, topped with malai and served in an unglazed clay kulhad that you smash afterwards.

places.name: Lassiwala
places.note: A Jaipur institution since 1944; check for the original stall, several imitators sit alongside.

places.name: Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB)
places.note: Sit-down alternative in the old city with lassi, kulfi and a huge sweet counter.

places.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
places.note: Good lassi to wash down the kachoris; busy from early morning.

food.name: Masala chai and thandai
food.desc: Cardamom-and-ginger chai poured all day, plus thandai - chilled milk with almonds, fennel and saffron, drunk in the summer heat.

places.name: Gulab Ji Chai Wala
places.note: Decades-old roadside chai stall that draws everyone from rickshaw drivers to politicians.

places.name: Sahu Chai Wala
places.note: Old-city tea stop known for strong, milky masala chai and bun maska.

places.name: Tapri Central
places.note: Rooftop tea cafe overlooking Central Park; dozens of teas and a young Jaipur crowd.

landmarks: Amber Fort
A majestic hilltop fort of honey-colored sandstone and marble overlooking Maota Lake, famed for its mirrored Sheesh Mahal and elephant-ride approach.
Hawa Mahal (Palace of the Winds)
A pink sandstone facade of 953 intricately latticed windows, built so royal women could observe street life unseen, now Jaipur's most photographed icon.
City Palace
A sprawling royal complex blending Rajput and Mughal architecture, still home to the former royal family and filled with courtyards, museums, and ornate gates.
Jantar Mantar
A UNESCO-listed collection of monumental 18th-century astronomical instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial, built by astronomer-king Jai Singh II.
Jal Mahal (Water Palace)
A dreamlike sandstone palace appearing to float in the middle of Man Sagar Lake, with four of its five floors submerged beneath the water.
Nahargarh Fort
A rugged fort perched on the Aravalli hills above Jaipur, offering the city's best sunset panoramas over the pink-hued rooftops below.
Albert Hall Museum
An ornate Indo-Saracenic sandstone building set in Ram Niwas Garden, showcasing Rajasthani art, textiles, and a famed ancient Egyptian mummy.
Jaigarh Fort
A formidable hilltop fortress built to protect Amber Fort, home to the world's largest wheeled cannon and sweeping views of the Pink City.
Patrika Gate
A vividly painted modern gateway at Jawahar Circle, its nine ornate arches and intricate murals celebrating Rajasthan's culture make it a vibrant photo magnet.
Galtaji (Monkey Temple)
A sacred pilgrimage site of ancient temples and natural springs tucked in a rocky gorge, populated by hundreds of free-roaming rhesus macaques.

train.note: No international trains. Jaipur Junction sits just west of the Pink City and is well served from Delhi - the Ajmer Shatabdi and the Vande Bharat take under four hours. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead; the Golden Triangle trains to Delhi and Agra are among India's busiest, and the luxury Palace on Wheels tourist train also starts here.

bus.note: No international coaches. RSRTC (https://rsrtconline.rajasthan.gov.in/) runs Volvo and ordinary buses from Sindhi Camp bus stand to Delhi (about 5-6 hours), Udaipur, Jodhpur and Agra, with private sleepers bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/). Sindhi Camp is central and walkable from the old city.

ferry.note: Jaipur is deep inland in semi-arid Rajasthan with no navigable water, so there are no ferries. The lake beside the Jal Mahal is ornamental and closed to boats.

half.name: Abhaneri (Chand Baori)
half.blurb: A deep stepwell of symmetrical zigzagging stairs in the village of Abhaneri, about ninety minutes from Jaipur.

full.name: Pushkar
full.blurb: A pilgrimage town built around a sacred lake and home to the only major Brahma temple in the world, about two and a half hours from Jaipur.

full.name: Ranthambore National Park
full.blurb: A former royal hunting ground turned tiger reserve, with jeep safaris through forest and ruined pavilions, roughly three and a half hours from Jaipur.

full.name: Taj Mahal (Agra)
full.blurb: The white marble mausoleum built by Shah Jahan, reached by a roughly four-hour drive or a faster express train from Jaipur.
